affected_cohort: Applicants for second or third Working Holiday Maker visas (subclasses 417 and 462); UK passport holders are exempt from the new registration/invitation process
mechanism: Registration opens 2026-12-01; from 2027-03-01 applicants must register, be selected and complete specified work before applying for another WHM visa. The second-visa specified-work requirement rises from 88 to 120 days; third-visa requirement is unchanged. Transitional direct applications remain available through 2027-02-28 for applicants meeting the specified work and lodgement conditions.
model_treatment: Temporary youth-mobility cohort only; not a skilled-worker, permanent-residence or general migration shock. No macro energy adjustment.
counterfactual_design: After 2027-03-01, compare second/third WHM application and completion outcomes with pre-change cohorts and comparable temporary-work cohorts; account for selection into invitation, origin-country agreements and seasonal labour demand; test pre-trends and placebo dates.
revision_note: Backfilled from the 2026-11-18 research report after checking the official 2026-11-17 Home Affairs notice; not a new 2026-11-19 policy announcement.
evidence_note: Official notice states registration opens 1 December 2026, first invitations expected mid-January 2027, new process effective 1 March 2027, and 120 days of specified work for a second WHM visa. Registering or receiving an invitation does not guarantee a visa.

affected_cohort: People making asylum claims inland or at a Canadian port of entry; eligible claimants seeking work permits
mechanism: Regulations introduced one online application process for inland and port-of-entry claims, clearer government review timelines, rules for reinstatement of withdrawn or abandoned claims, support for vulnerable claimants and access to work permits for eligible claims.
model_treatment: Humanitarian/asylum cohort only; retain separately from voluntary labour, study and skilled migration flows. No macro energy adjustment.
counterfactual_design: A future event study could examine processing times, claim abandonment/reinstatement and work-permit access before and after 2026-11-03, stratified by inland/port-of-entry and claimant type; composition changes and concurrent statutory changes require controls and sensitivity tests.
revision_note: Backfilled from the 2026-11-18 research report; official IRCC release and effective date rechecked on 2026-11-19.
evidence_note: IRCC states the regulations came into force 3 November 2026. The release also reports asylum claims fell 52% Jan-Aug 2026 versus 2025; this is a descriptive comparison, not an effect estimate.

affected_cohort: Workers in 17 specified Tier 2 Green List occupations, including telecommunications technicians and listed trades/technicians; existing Work to Residence applicants meeting transitional conditions
mechanism: Seventeen occupations move out of Tier 2 Work to Residence because new Skilled Migrant Category pathways cover them. Some may qualify through SMC with different wage, qualification and work-experience rules; Green List labour-market-test exemptions and priority processing for job checks/AEWV will no longer apply to the removed roles. Transitional arrangements preserve qualifying work already accumulated for eligible applicants.
model_treatment: Occupation-specific pathway substitution. Direction is mixed and depends on SMC eligibility; do not generalise to all skilled migrants or technology workers. No macro energy adjustment.
counterfactual_design: After 2027-03-08, compare affected occupations with similar unaffected occupations on residence applications, time to residence and job-check outcomes; control for SMC pathway changes, employer demand and transitional eligibility; test pre-trends and occupation-specific shocks.
revision_note: Backfilled from the 2026-11-18 research report and rechecked against the official INZ notice on 2026-11-19.
evidence_note: The official notice names 17 occupations and states the new settings begin 8 March 2027. Some experienced workers may have more accessible SMC routes, but not all will qualify.

affected_cohort: APEC Business Travel Card holders with Hong Kong pre-clearance visiting for short-term business
mechanism: Maximum visa-free stay in Hong Kong for pre-cleared ABTC holders increased from 60 to 90 days; other entry arrangements remain unchanged.
model_treatment: Business-visitor mobility only; not a work, residence or permanent-residence pathway. No macro energy adjustment.
counterfactual_design: If relevant, compare short-term business-visitor duration and repeat visits for ABTC holders with comparable non-ABTC business visitors before and after 2026-11-01; selection into ABTC and concurrent APEC changes limit causal interpretation.
revision_note: Backfilled from the 2026-11-18 research report; official Immigration Department release rechecked on 2026-11-19.
evidence_note: Hong Kong's Immigration Department confirms the 90-day period from 1 November 2026 for ABTC holders with HKSAR pre-clearance. This does not confer residence or employment rights.

effective_date: Not yet specified; further technical and operational guidance is to be published before implementation
affected_cohort: Applicants seeking settlement on routes within the Earned Settlement framework, including relevant work and family routes; separate transitional and protected cohorts apply
mechanism: Government response sets a 10-year default pathway, with 5-year settlement for qualifying higher earners (at least GBP 50,271 in three of five years) and 3-year settlement for the highest earners (at least GBP 125,141 in three of four years). It also sets minimum contribution, character, no-government-debt, B2 English and Life in the UK requirements; temporary routes such as Student and Graduate no longer count towards settlement under the framework; the Long Residence route closes. Specified breaches can lead to a 20-year path. Targeted transitional treatment is retained for certain pre-May-2025 care workers and other defined groups.
model_treatment: Major settlement-friction and time-to-residence policy feature, but announced framework only. Preserve route/cohort-specific rules and implementation uncertainty; no macro energy change until commencement, transition rules and applicant-level eligibility are known.
counterfactual_design: After commencement, compare settlement application/approval and time-to-settlement outcomes across affected routes and protected/transitional cohorts; use pre-reform cohorts and unaffected routes as controls only after testing parallel trends, composition, income selection and route switching. No causal claim from announcement alone.
revision_note: New manual-review event from the 2026-11-19 review of the official Home Office consultation outcome; implementation date not stated.
evidence_note: The 12 November 2026 government response is a final framework, but the page says further guidance will precede implementation. The consultation received 204,667 responses; respondents were self-selecting, so this is not a representative public-opinion survey.

affected_cohort: Express Entry researcher category candidates; university professors and lecturers (NOC 41200) with qualifying Canadian work experience or job offers paid by Canadian entities through stipends/grants/bursaries/scholarships; post-secondary teaching and research assistants (NOC 41201) are excluded from this category
mechanism: Eligible non-wage compensation is now recognized for specified professor/lecturer work experience and job offers; NOC 41201 teaching and research assistant experience is no longer eligible under the Researchers with Canadian work experience category.
model_treatment: Narrow category-based selection shock for researchers/academics, not a general software-engineering or all-skilled-worker change. No macro energy adjustment.
counterfactual_design: Potential event study comparing NOC 41200 with adjacent academic occupations and the removed NOC 41201 group before and after 2026-11-17; test pre-trends, category selection, job-offer composition and concurrent Express Entry point changes.
revision_note: New policy event identified during 2026-11-19 review of the current IRCC Express Entry change page.
evidence_note: IRCC states the researcher-category changes came into effect 17 November 2026. This is not a broad change to Express Entry eligibility for all applicants.

affected_cohort: Parents and other secondary applicants in resident visa applications where a dependent child is unlawfully in New Zealand; applications made before 2026-11-12 retain previous rules
mechanism: Parents and secondary applicants will not be granted residence while a dependent child remains unlawfully in New Zealand; applicants are given an opportunity to respond before a final decision, and special-circumstances appeals remain possible.
model_treatment: Family/dependant eligibility and settlement-cohesion feature for a narrow affected cohort; do not generalise to single applicants or all New Zealand residence applications. No macro energy adjustment.
counterfactual_design: Compare affected family applications lodged just before and after 2026-11-12 with otherwise similar families whose dependent children maintain lawful status; account for route, child age/health and application composition; test pre-trends and transitional cut-off sensitivity.
revision_note: New policy event identified during 2026-11-19 review of the official INZ notice.
evidence_note: INZ published the change on 10 November and applies it to resident visa applications made from 12 November 2026; earlier applications remain under prior rules.

effective_date: Not stated in the official release; implementation detail and operational pathway guidance pending
affected_cohort: Indian and Swiss nationals covered by the bilateral Migration and Mobility Partnership and young-professional training-exchange agreement; specific eligibility and quotas not yet stated in the release
mechanism: The agreement formalises migration cooperation, education/science/labour exchanges and legal mobility pathways; it also covers readmission and cooperation against irregular migration, trafficking and document forgery. A separate exchange agreement enables young people from either country to undertake training placements in the other.
model_treatment: Bilateral origin-destination policy feature for India-Switzerland; potentially reduces legal-mobility friction for specified cohorts, but no quantitative or route-level change is assigned until implementation details and take-up data are available.
counterfactual_design: After operational guidance and outcomes are published, compare India-Switzerland eligible mobility/training cohorts with matched country pairs or unaffected cohorts; account for pre-existing mobility, selection, education and labour-market trends; test pre-trends and placebo dates.
revision_note: Backfilled during 2026-11-19 review; official SEM release dated 5 October 2026. Not a new 19 November announcement.
evidence_note: SEM confirms two agreements were concluded during the 5 October presidential visit. The release does not provide commencement date, visa quota or detailed eligibility criteria.
